correctness.rationale: The proof constructs the baseline ordinary birth chain, computes finite marked-last probability from exact exponential races, represents slow infection through a conditional integrated hazard, establishes its limiting time by concentration and Riemann-sum arguments, and couples ordinary completion between ordinary-only and initially marked-infected chains. Both have 2 log N leading completion time. The critical expectation follows from a separate uniform L^2 bound via the half-population hitting time. Boundary cases are proved on their stated scales. 44 exact rational finite-state checks passed for N=3..13, though those finite tests alone are not asymptotic proofs.

originality.rationale: Checked exact claim, aliases and stronger implications against indexed results and the substantive primary full texts of Janson (1999), Aalto–Leskelä (2015), and Leskelä–Ngo (2018/2019). Their regular iid passage weights, transmitter-dependent contacts with uniformly selected recipients, and sparse-graph additive boundary delays respectively exclude the distinguished receiver edge-rate weakening that creates the present mixed logarithmic completion law. Closest indexed double-star and clique-bouquet results differ in structural model and do not imply this exact finite-size gamma ratio or its marked-receiver crossover. A general prior theorem on all inhomogeneous edge-weighted complete graphs, if present, could subsume the result; no historical-priority certification is claimed. Peterson (2010/2011) is an especially close edge-rate factorization but studies SIS with positive recovery and extinction/quasi-stationary observables, not SI full-infection times.
residual_risks: An unlocated prior inhomogeneous complete-graph SI/FPP theorem or exact gamma-ratio table could subsume the calculation.
The 2018 sparse-graph paper is comparative literature, not a focal archive-period source; the focal archived first-public evidence is the 1999 Janson publication.
No independent scientific audit or exhaustive priority certification has been performed.

value.rationale: Recipient-specific weakness is a motivated perturbation of a canonical kinetic infection network. The exact finite gamma law and a three-regime crossover at rho_N~1/log N identify when one resistant vertex overwhelms the homogeneous network flooding time. The atom-plus-exponential critical law and an explicit nonzero expected-time penalty are structural dynamical observables, not a cosmetic parameter substitution. A useful benchmark for heterogeneity and completion-extreme behavior is provided without claiming a general-network theorem.
